title: 360 Kidnapping of Daung Chi Sing

The following is the rough translation of the copies
of documents, statement, etc., re the kidnapping of
Daung Chi Sing (唐璇星 ):-

To Military Court,
According to a report from Bang Yih 彭澤,
the secret service agent of the Central Government,
Daung Chi Sing, a rebel leader, was arrested at 10
p.m. last night at Yung Hsing Lee 永興里 4th
district, Chapei, and was detained in the Station of
that district. The prisoner being important, I was re-
quested to send him secretly to Peking.
Apart from telegraphing to the Generalissimo's
Office, I have detailed two detectives named Har Yao
Kwong 郝耀光 and Wang Pao Tuh 王寶德, and 12
Police Constables to escort the prisoner to the capital.
They will leave this evening by train. Your Honourable
Court is requested to receive the prisoner with
compliments.
(Signed) Yang Siu Tuh. 楊善德
____________________

To Military Court,
Daung Chi Sing, a Cantonese rebel,
has had his headquarters in Shanghai for a long time,
and has been a disturber of the peace. According
to a telegram from General Yang the said prisoner
was living in Frenchtown, and was enticed to Chapei
where he was arrested. As the prisoner could not
be tried in Shanghai, the Police were directed to
send him to Your Honourable Court under an escort
of two detectives and 12 P.C.s Besides giving an
answer to General Yang, we (Generalissimo's Office)
send you this letter. The said prisoner having
lived in the Settlement, the foreigners might make
trouble if they knew of his arrest. For this reason
his sentence should not be made public. Moreover
Daung has many followers so the case should be kept
very secret. All leakage of news to the press should
be prevented in order to avoid complication.
(Sealed) Generalissimo's Office)
____________________

To Military Court,
Referring to the case of Daung Chi
Sing, this office knew that he would deny his offences
and a telegram has already been sent to General Yang
directing him to investigate the charge against the
prisoner. Now a report has been received from the
General according to which the prisoner is a
rebel leader. He plotted to cause dissension in
the capital and provinces. He is the chief instigator
of the "Chohc" incident. According to a report from
a foreigner the prisoner concealed arms and ammunitions
in the vicinity of Tsunfming. Besides, he sent
threatening letters to residents in order to extort
money. Once he called at the accountant's office
of a certain bank and demanded money from a Cantonese
whom he threatened. He also used the name of Tang
Shao Yi to swindle money. He established the Min Kuo
Pao (Republican Daily News), in which he published
seditious news. Acting on instructions from Yang
Tcheng, Bang Yih (agent of the secret service) has

以下是关于唐璇星（Daung Chi Sing）绑架案的文件副本、陈述书等的粗略译文：-

致军事法庭，
据中央政府密探彭澤（Bang Yih）报告，叛乱首领唐璇星于昨晚10时在闸北第四区永興里被捕，并拘押在该区警署。因该囚犯身份重要，本人奉命将其秘密送往北京。
除已向大元帅府发电报外，本人已指派两名名为郝耀光（Har Yao Kwong）和王寶德（Wang Pao Tuh）的侦探，以及12名巡捕，护送该囚犯前往首都。他们将于今晚乘火车出发。敬请贵庭惠予接收该囚犯为荷。
（签名）楊善德
___

致军事法庭，
广东籍叛乱分子唐璇星长期以上海为总部，一直扰乱治安。据杨将军电报称，该囚犯原居住在法租界，后被诱至闸北并在那里被捕。由于该囚犯无法在上海受审，警方奉命在两名侦探和12名巡捕的护送下，将其送交贵庭。除回复杨将军外，我们（大元帅府）特致此函。鉴于该囚犯曾居住在租界，若外国人得知其被捕，可能会制造麻烦。因此，其判决不应公开。此外，唐氏拥有众多追随者，故本案应严格保密。应防止向新闻界泄露任何消息，以避免复杂化。
（盖章）大元帅府
___

致军事法庭，
关于唐璇星一案，本府知悉他将否认其罪行，并已致电杨将军，指示其调查对该囚犯的指控。现收到杨将军的报告，称该囚犯为叛乱首领。他策划在京师及各省制造分裂。他是“肇和”事件的主要煽动者。据一名外国人报告，该囚犯在崇明附近藏匿武器弹药。此外，他还向居民寄送恐吓信以勒索钱财。他曾前往某银行的会计室，向一名受其威胁的广东人索要钱财。他还冒用唐绍仪的名义诈骗钱财。他创办了《民国报》（Min Kuo Pao），并在其中刊登煽动性新闻。根据杨澄的命令，密探彭澤（Bang Yih）已

No. ____ 360
Date ____ 14/3/16

made investigations and confirmed these allegation. Bang
has now departed for Peking regarding this case. It is
believed that, although the prisoner is very cunning, he
cannot deny. Rear-Admiral Tsai Ting Han 蔡廷幹 knows
Bang's address.
(Sealed) Generalissimo's Office.
Dated 12/3/16.

To Generalissimo's Office,
According to the statement
made by Daung Chi Sing, he graduated in England during
the Ching dynasty. Since the inauguration of the
Republic he did not interfere in politics, and has
been living in Shanghai for three years during which
time he did not take part in revolutionary affairs.
Being an old rebel, he knew everything about the
revolutionary business. As he was arrested through
a trap laid for him by his 1st cousin, he does not
care whether lives and dies. In case the Government
employs him, he is willing to give some information
which he knows. Prior to the disturbance in Yunnan
news of the matter **〔此处转录不清〕** reached **〔此处转录不清〕**. Yunnan was in need
of three things, viz military force, finance and
munitions. Although the disturbance started in
Yunnan three months ago the rebels cannot continue
the struggle, and there are only a few people who
are trying to support it. These are planning to
attack Fokien and then Kiangsi. If they are
successful they will than invade either Kiangsu or
Hunan. The Manchu Restoration Party are attempting
to capture Shantung and Three Eastern Provinces with
the assistance of the Japanese. The latter movement
was deferred owing to the non-arrival of munitions.
It is reported that munitions were sent to Hai Kou 海口
from Germany three months ago. If the Government
cannot prevent the arrival of these munitions or
buy them, they may be delivered to the rebels.
Recently the British merchants suggested to ask the
rebels to buy the munitions in order to prevent
them from being smuggled to India. I did not
buy these munitions, and neither did I conceal them
in the vicinity of Tsungming. Recently Tang Hu
Loong 湯化龍 arrived at Shanghai and attempted to
instigate the Navy to join his side. His mission
succeeded but Chen Chi Mei, being jealous of Tang's
merits, sent men to raid the "Choho." The time of
the raid made by Chen's men not being the time agreed
to with Tang, the other warships did not render their
support. Truly this raid was not made at my instigation,
and I am not connected with the threatening of the
Cantonese merchants, etc.
It is ascertained that notwithstanding the fact
that the prisoner denied his offence, he knew everything
of the revolutionary movements. Would anybody believe
that he is not a leader of the rebels' party? Moreover
a circular warrant for his arrest is kept on record.
Therefore the prisoner, in accordance with Article 101
of the New Criminal Code, shall be executed. Your
approval of this sentence is awaited and the statement
of the prisoner is herewith enclosed.
(Sealed) Military Court.

进行调查并证实了这些指控。彭现已就此案启程前往北京。相信尽管该囚犯非常狡猾，但他无法抵赖。海军少将蔡廷幹知道彭的地址。
（盖章）大元帅府。
日期 1916年3月12日。

致大元帅府，
根据唐璇星的陈述，他在清朝时期毕业于英国。自民国成立以来，他未干涉政治，并在上海居住了三年，在此期间未参与革命事务。作为一名老资格的叛乱分子，他对革命事务了如指掌。由于他是被其堂兄设下的陷阱所捕，他对生死已置之度外。如果政府任用他，他愿意提供其所知的一些情报。在云南骚乱之前，有关此事的消息**〔此处转录不清〕**传到了**〔此处转录不清〕**。云南需要三样东西，即军事力量、财政和军火。虽然骚乱始于三个月前的云南，但叛乱分子无法继续斗争，只有少数人试图支持它。这些人正计划进攻福建，然后进攻江西。如果他们成功，随后进攻江苏或湖南。满清复辟派正试图在日本人的协助下夺取山东和东三省。后一行动因军火未运到而推迟。据报道，三个月前从德国向海口运送了军火。如果政府不能阻止这些军火运抵或将其买下，它们可能会被交付给叛乱分子。最近，英国商人建议让叛乱分子购买这些军火，以防止它们被走私到印度。我并未购买这些军火，也未将它们藏在崇明附近。最近湯化龍（Tang Hu Loong）抵达上海，试图煽动海军加入其阵营。他的使命成功了，但陈其美因嫉妒唐的功劳，派人袭击了“肇和”舰。由于陈氏手下发动袭击的时间并非与唐约定的时间，其他军舰未提供支援。确实，这次袭击并非由我煽动，我也与恐吓广东商人等事无关。
经查实，尽管该囚犯否认其罪行，但他对革命运动的一切了如指掌。谁会相信他不是叛乱党派的首领呢？此外，档案中存有对他的通缉令。因此，根据《新刑律》第101条，该囚犯应被处决。待批准此判决，随函附上该囚犯的陈述书。
（盖章）军事法庭。

Translation of a Permit Issued by the Peking Military
Court to remove Body of a Rebel named Daung Chi Sing ( 唐继星 )

P e r m i t .

As a rule the families of persons executed by order of
the Peking Military Court are allowed to remove the bodies.
This Court now hereby issues this permit to Daung Bah ( 唐坂 )
to remove the remains of Daung Chi Sing ( 唐继星 ) from this
City for burial. The persons carrying the remains should be
allowed to pass freely on production of this permit.

Issued to Daung Bah.
Dated 27th day, 4th month, 5th year of the Republic of China.
This permit is to be returned for cancellation within three
days.

北京军事法庭签发的移除名为唐继星（Daung Chi Sing）的叛乱分子尸体的许可证译文

许 可 证 。

按照惯例，经北京军事法庭命令处决之人的家属获准移走尸体。本庭特此颁发此许可证给唐坂（Daung Bah），准许其将唐继星（Daung Chi Sing）的遗体移出本市安葬。持此许可证者，携运遗体人员应获准自由通行。

发给唐坂。
中华民国五年四月二十七日。
此许可证须在三天内交回注销。
